### Description of the bug:


8.5.0. 8.5.1 and probably other <9 versions of bazel can crash `bazel coverage` on `rules_kotlin` targets with `rules_java 9.3.0`

Don't have a full self-contained repro or possible workaround yet, but basically getting
```
Caused by: java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError: Exception java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: org/jacoco/agent/rt/internal_4742761/Offline [in thread "main"]
```
from `bazel coverage` on kotlin targets with rules_java 9.3.0

Which boils down to
  • Instrumentation uses JaCoCo 0.8.11, which has org/jacoco/agent/rt/internal_4742761/Offline.class
  • Runtime uses JaCoCo 0.8.14, which has org/jacoco/agent/rt/internal_29a6edd/Offline.class

rules_kotlin does directly reference jacoco via
https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_kotlin/blob/b4122754897017dfdbba842038f1c384fec78d5a/kotlin/internal/toolchains.bzl#L198
https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_kotlin/blob/b4122754897017dfdbba842038f1c384fec78d5a/MODULE.release.bazel#L21
and does point to older rules_java in https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel-central-registry/blob/main/modules/rules_kotlin/2.2.2/MODULE.bazel
but patching it to be 9.3.0 with `common --registry=file:///%workspace%/bazel-local-registry --registry https://bcr.bazel.build` doesn't seem to help

`external/rules_jvm_external++maven+jacoco/BUILD` location shows up as the place still defining 0.8.11 so could potentially be some other module clashing on rules_jvm_external maven.install name and winning by chance/order bringing an old version in. But didn't manage to confirm or find a definition for this external repo. https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/release-8.5.1/tools/jdk/BUILD.java_tools also defines 0.8.11 but looks a bit different

Java Rules

comments.body:
Sounds like this might be https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_java/issues/202

For a failing target, can you see if `bazel query 'deps(//target)'` has jacoco in there? If it does, `bazel query 'somepath(//target, //the/jacoco/target)'` should tell you where it's coming from.

edit: s/blaze/bazel

> coverage with rules_java 9.2.0 works

Thanks, this was important to know, will look into this now

One more thing I'm trying to investigate - this file https://github.com/jongerrish/rules_kotlin/blob/770b23ebacff603e568efb65088f6b444d65900c/src/main/kotlin/io/bazel/kotlin/builder/tasks/jvm/JacocoInstrumentation.kt in `rules_kotlin` imports jacoco, but I don't yet see where it gets it from, and which version is used when it fails

Actually when I build it (`bazel build //src/main/kotlin/io/bazel/kotlin/builder/tasks:foo_deploy.jar --sandbox_debug` in rules_kotlin) and intentionally break syntax in JacocoInstrumentation.kt to get compile env with `--sandbox_debug` then I can check version of jacoco
```console
$ jar tf ..sandbox_path../linux-sandbox/1029/execroot/_main/bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/external/rules_java++toolchains+remote_java_tools/_ijar/jacoco_coverage_runner/rules_java++toolchains+remote_java_tools/java_tools/JacocoCoverage_jarjar_deploy-ijar.jar | grep Offline.class
org/jacoco/agent/rt/internal_4742761/Offline.class
# and if I bump MODULE.bazel rules_java to 9.3.0 in rules_kotlin then org/jacoco/agent/rt/internal_29a6edd/Offline.class
```

Now the question for a workaround is how can I make this bump when consuming rules_kotlin, I had an attempt via registry override but it didn't work 🤔 

And another question is why it diverges and what''s the proper way to handle that (rule making compile-time instrumentation and bazel/rules_java providing runtime, or whole approach can be changed?)?
Related: #21813 ~https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_java/issues/202~ (I'm blind, already linked to above)

Got something here
```console
$ bazel build @@rules_kotlin+//src/main/kotlin:build_deploy.jar
$ jar tf bazel-bin/external/rules_kotlin+/src/main/kotlin/build_deploy.jar | grep Offline.class
org/jacoco/agent/rt/internal_4742761/Offline.class
org/jacoco/agent/rt/internal_29a6edd/Offline.class

$ jar xf bazel-bin/external/rules_kotlin+/src/main/kotlin/build_deploy.jar META-INF/maven/org.jacoco/org.jacoco.core/pom.properties
$ cat META-INF/maven/org.jacoco/org.jacoco.core/pom.properties 
artifactId=org.jacoco.core
groupId=org.jacoco
version=0.8.11
```
And so far I get this output regardless of rules_java version or attempts at bump it in rules_kotlin via local registry
AFAICT things should work fine the way rules_kotlin setups up it's dependencies on Jacoco. Is there something special in the way your target(s) are set up?

Created a repro repo https://github.com/dmivankov/bug_reports/tree/java93_kotlin_coverage
Looks like issue is likely within kotlin_worker compilation, will try to force it being built against newer jacoco

Still confusing, possibly around bzlmod. In `rules_kotlin` repo changing `rules_java` version to 9.3.0 and
```console
$ bazel build //src/main/kotlin/io/bazel/kotlin/builder/cmd:build_deploy.jar
$ jar tf bazel-bin/src/main/kotlin/io/bazel/kotlin/builder/cmd/build_deploy.jar | grep Offline.class
```
results in getting either 0.8.11 or 0.8.14 package name for this file as expected

But with https://github.com/dmivankov/bug_reports/commit/1f9ac23f1bd4567b6e0a1faee59349a56385ce0f registry override two versions are pulled into jar and I can't find where the second comes from, other than
```
    jars = ["java_tools/third_party/java/jacoco/org.jacoco.agent-0.8.11.jar"],
    srcjar = "java_tools/third_party/java/jacoco/org.jacoco.agent-0.8.11-sources.jar",
    jars = ["java_tools/third_party/java/jacoco/org.jacoco.core-0.8.11.jar"],
    srcjar = "java_tools/third_party/java/jacoco/org.jacoco.core-0.8.11-sources.jar",
    srcs = ["java_tools/third_party/java/jacoco/org.jacoco.core-0.8.11.jar"],
    jars = ["java_tools/third_party/java/jacoco/org.jacoco.report-0.8.11.jar"],
    srcjar = "java_tools/third_party/java/jacoco/org.jacoco.report-0.8.11-sources.jar",
    jars = ["java_tools/third_party/java/jacoco/jacocoagent-0.8.11.jar"],
    jars = ["java_tools/third_party/java/jacoco/jacocoagent-0.8.11.jar"],
in external/bazel_tools/tools/jdk/BUILD.java_tools
```
but those jars don't seem to be used at build time or materialized, best guess is it somehow comes from bazel binary itself

This is a rules_kotlin issue. 

The kotlin builder being used for `KotlinCompile` is a jar that is packaged at release time, and contains the jacoco classes. One can confirm this by fetching the latest release tar.gz at https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_kotlin/releases/tag/v2.2.2 and inspecting the contents of `src/main/kotlin/kotlin_worker.jar` in it. 

Thus, the jacoco version used for instrumentation will depend on the the version of rules_java in rules_kotlin at time of release. 

ISTM these classes should never end up in the `kotlin_worker.jar`

Right, so it is pre-built, will open an issue against rules_kotlin. I guess easy way to fix is get away from pre-compiled worker, and probably harder is to pre-build for multiple jacoco versions and select based on project rules_java/jacoco version.

So will close this one, open new in rules_kotlin, will try to play with non-prebuilt approach, and if getting jacoco version isn't easy then may open a ticket on bazel or rules_java side to expose the info and/or jacoco lib matching the runtime 👍
